papers.title_en: Anatomically Conditioned Recurrent Refinement for Topology-Aware Circle of Willis Segmentation
papers.authors: Juraj Perić, Marija Habijan, Dario Mužević, Irena Galić, Danilo Babin, Aleksandra Pižurica
papers.evidence: 在MRA图像上使用监督U-Net变体分割Willis环。
papers.tldr: Willis环是颅内重要血管结构，MRA分割中因血管纤细、拓扑复杂，传统CNN常产生断裂伪影，破坏结构连贯性。我们提出解剖条件循环细化U-Net（AC2RUNet），将网络解耦为静态解剖流和动态拓扑优化流，通过循环迭代逐步矫正分割错误，并采用课程学习从高召回几何监督过渡到拓扑感知约束。在TopCoW多中心数据上，AC2RUNet将Hausdorff距离从nnU-Net的9.17mm降至4.72mm，Betti数误差从0.40降至0.19，同时体积Dice保持相当。该模型显著提升血管连通性，有效克服断裂问题，为拓扑敏感的脑动脉分割提供了新方案。
papers.abstract_en: Segmenting the Circle of Willis (CoW) from Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) is challenging due to complex topology and thin vascular structures that are prone to fragmentation. Standard Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) often fail to capture these topological constraints, resulting in "broken vessel" artifacts. To address this, we propose the Anatomically Conditioned Recurrent Refinement U-Net (AC2RUNet). Our architecture decouples segmentation into two streams: a Static Stream that extracts invariant anatomical features and a lightweight Dynamic Stream that iteratively refines topological errors over time. We further introduce a dynamic curriculum learning strategy that transitions from high-recall geometric supervision to topology-aware constraints. Validated on the TopCoW dataset, AC2RUNet substantially reduces Hausdorff Distance (4.72 mm vs 9.17 mm) and Betti number errors (0.19 vs 0.40), improving topological connectivity over the nnU-Net baseline while maintaining comparable volumetric Dice.

papers.title_en: Point Cloud Segmentation for Autonomous Clip Positioning in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy on a Phantom
papers.authors: Balázs Gyenes, Nikolai Franke, Paul Maria Scheikl, Pit Henrich, Rayan Younis, Gerhard Neumann, Martin Wagner, Franziska Mathis-Ullrich
papers.evidence: 腹腔镜手术中基于全监督点云分割的自主操作。
papers.tldr: 机器人辅助手术要求高精度和可解释性，但数据稀缺限制模型训练。本研究针对腹腔镜胆囊切除术仿体，提出基于点云分割和样条插值的自主夹子定位系统。通过合成数据预训练和两种新颖数据增强技术，在仅60个真实点云上训练模型。系统实现0.75mm定位精度，95%成功率，自主夹子定位成功率100%。这是首个在物理仿体上演示自主夹子定位的系统，方法可推广至其他需精确定位和导航的手术与非手术任务。
papers.abstract_en: High-risk applications in robotics, such as robot-assisted surgery, present unique challenges. These systems must be both highly precise and interpretable in order to be deployed in environments with very low tolerance for error or unsafe exploration. We present the first robotic system to demonstrate autonomous clip positioning on a physical phantom in laparoscopic surgery, one of the most common interventions in general surgery. After segmentation of a colorless point cloud from a single camera, target positions for the clips are extracted using spline interpolation, and can then be adjusted by the human operator. The segmentation model is trained on only 60 hand-labeled real point clouds, reflecting data scarcity in the surgical domain. We overcome this with a combination of pre-training on 128,000 synthetic point clouds and two novel data augmentation techniques. The motion of the end-effector to each target is visualized for the operator, satisfying the unique motion constraints of minimally-invasive surgery while ensuring that the robot's actions are verifiable and interpretable. In real robot experiments, our system localizes targets with the required precision of 0.75mm at a 95% success rate and executes autonomous clip positioning with a 100% success rate. We provide insights that are applicable to many other surgical and non-surgical tasks that require identifying and navigating to a precise target. Source code and project page: https://github.com/balazsgyenes/kirurc
